annihilate

uh-NY-uh-layt -- from Latin ad- ('to') + nihil ('nothing') + -ate: literally 'to reduce to nothing.' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To annihilate is to destroy completely, often violently -- typically defeating an organized or living opponent so thoroughly that they cannot recover.

In the finals, the top-seeded chess prodigy annihilated her opponent, winning in under twenty moves.

Worked Example

In the championship debate, the returning state finalist dismantled every single one of her opponent's arguments point by point, leaving him with nothing left to say by the final round.

That kind of total, crushing defeat of a rival -- not just winning, but leaving them with nothing -- is exactly what it means to annihilate an opponent.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

vanquish: To vanquish is to conquer an enemy completely, with a grand, storybook tone -- knights vanquish dragons, armies vanquish invaders. Annihilate is just as total but darker, stressing destruction so thorough the loser cannot rebuild. Vanquish suits epic, high-stakes showdowns; no one vanquishes a rival in a Tuesday scrimmage.

trounce: To trounce is to beat an opponent soundly, usually in a game or contest with a lopsided score -- yet the loser walks away and plays again next week. To annihilate goes much further: the defeat is so complete that nothing is left to rebuild. Trounce embarrasses an opponent; annihilate finishes one.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

spare: to refrain from harming or defeating someone

concede: to admit defeat or give up a point to an opponent

Where it sits · how total the defeat is — crush → annihilate → exterminate

crush vs. annihilate: To crush a rival is to win decisively -- a common, slightly informal word for a one-sided victory -- but a crushed team can regroup and come back. Annihilate is stronger and more absolute: the defeat is total, with nothing left to fight back with.

exterminate vs. annihilate: Exterminate goes even further than annihilate. To annihilate an opponent is to defeat them so thoroughly they cannot recover; to exterminate is to wipe out every last member, so that nothing survives at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — an-

prefix — an-: to, toward (variant of Latin ad-)

root — -nihil-

root — -nihil-: nothing (Latin (nihil))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make, to cause to become (Latin (-are))

Put it together

Put it together: Annihilate comes from Latin ad- ('to') -- here spelled an- -- plus nihil ('nothing') plus -ate ('to make') -- so to annihilate something is literally to reduce it to nothing at all.

Use the root in a new word: nihilism

Use the root in a new word: nihilism: The philosophy professor spent the whole lecture explaining nihilism, the belief that life has no inherent meaning or value.

Root Check

Word Choice

Annihilate usually describes utterly defeating a living or organized opponent -- an army, a team, a debate rival -- unlike obliterate, taught earlier in this unit, which usually describes erasing a thing or a trace rather than defeating someone.
